notes: Large-source-unit candidate checked: אֲשֶׁר עַל־כֵּן → *Because* is genuinely indivisible. The one English word carries the relative's subordination and the causal force of עַל־כֵּן together, no morpheme owns a part of it, and splitting it would leave two of the three morphemes unrepresented beside a third holding the whole word, which rule 30 forbids. No morpheme's own lexeme is written in *Because*, so rule 6's first-token anchor gives the source head.
מֵאַחֲרָיו is split rather than fused, since the ASV writes a word for each morpheme (*from following*), which is rule 30's מִפְּנֵי → *from before* case.
